_about: Fictional source documents for editorial quality-gate tests. Publishers, companies, and figures are invented.

vendor_launch.title: Lumen Labs releases Lumen-4 math tutoring model
vendor_launch.body: Lumen Labs released Lumen-4, a math tutoring model, on Monday. The company says Lumen-4 solves 82% of competition math problems and is its most capable model to date.

independent_eval.title: Independent benchmark: Lumen-4 solves 61% of held-out problems
independent_eval.body: The Open Evaluation Collective tested Lumen-4 on 1,200 held-out competition math problems and found it solved 61% of them, below the 82% figure in Lumen Labs' announcement. The evaluators said the gap may reflect differences between test sets.

independent_eval_2.title: Second lab finds Lumen-4 strong on algebra, weaker on geometry
independent_eval_2.body: A second evaluation by the Northfield AI Lab found Lumen-4 solved 64% of algebra problems but only 48% of geometry problems. The lab disputed Lumen Labs' claim that the model is its most capable for every topic.

preprint.title: Evaluating Lumen-4 on held-out competition problems
preprint.body: We evaluate Lumen-4 on 1,200 held-out competition math problems drawn from 2024 and 2025 contests. The model solves 61% of them. This manuscript has been posted for comment.

bank_note.title: Harbor Bank: AI portfolio agents beat a 60/40 portfolio in a 20-year backtest
bank_note.body: Harbor Bank researchers reported that AI portfolio agents beat a 60/40 portfolio by 1.8 percentage points a year in a backtest covering 2005 to 2025, assuming trading costs of 0.1% per trade. The authors cautioned that an in-sample result is not proof of future outperformance.

finance_news.title: Harbor Bank's AI agents: a backtest, not a live track record
finance_news.body: Harbor Bank's result comes from a backtest, not a live track record. The bank has not reported live results for the agents, which it says remain a research project.

learning_study.title: AI tutoring and algebra outcomes in ninth grade
learning_study.body: In a randomized study of 600 ninth-grade students in 12 schools, students who used an AI tutor for eight weeks scored 4 points higher on an algebra test than a comparison group. The study did not measure transfer to unfamiliar problems.
